title: Cilium Envoy DaemonSet on by default — one more Pod per node

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only); the chart writes external-envoy-proxy on every install

quote: Cilium Envoy DaemonSet is now enabled by default for new installation if the helm attribute `envoy.enabled` is not specified
remediation: If cilium-config shows `external-envoy-proxy: "false"` and you do not set `envoy.enabled` or `upgradeCompatibility`, the 1.16 chart adds the cilium-envoy DaemonSet: one more Pod on every node, and a node already at its Pod limit evicts a non-critical Pod. Set `upgradeCompatibility=1.15` (or `envoy.enabled=false`) to keep the embedded proxy, or check node Pod headroom first.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(external-envoy-proxy)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # false means the upgrade adds a DaemonSet unless envoy.enabled is pinned

title: tcx BPF links by default on kernels 6.6+ — conflicts with third-party tc BPF programs

detection.reason: which other tc BPF programs run on a node is not collected

quote: For Linux kernels of version 6.6 or newer, Cilium by default switches to tcx BPF links
remediation: On the nodes named (kernel 6.6+), if anything else attaches old-style tc BPF programs (other CNIs in chaining mode, observability agents, DDoS tools), set Helm `bpf.enableTCX=false` before upgrading so Cilium keeps the old attachment mode. On EKS with Cilium chained to the AWS VPC CNI, the VPC CNI network-policy agent is one: with `--enable-network-policy=true` (the `aws-eks-nodeagent` container of `aws-node`, listed by the command) it attaches classic tc programs to every pod's host-side veth.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name) \(.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion)"'; kubectl get daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata as $m | .spec.template.spec.containers[]? | select(any(.args[]?; test("^--enable-network-policy=true$"))) | "\($m.namespace)/\($m.name) \(.name) enable-network-policy=true"'  # nodes on kernel 6.6+ switch to tcx; an aws-node row means the VPC CNI network-policy agent attaches old-style tc programs there

title: toFQDNs implementation overhauled — follow the upgrade guidance to avoid drops

detection.reason: read from the agent's Cilium projection (feature names, never the policy's values); needs Cilium collection switched on in Integrations

quote: The implementation of `toFQDNs` selectors in policies has been overhauled to improve performance
remediation: Clusters with toFQDNs policies (listed by the command) migrate their FQDN state on upgrade AND downgrade. Follow the upgrade note's instruction to avoid drops during the upgrade, and do not roll back through a version that predates the new implementation without reading the downgrade note.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; (.toFQDNs // []) | length != 0)) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a policy with toFQDNs rules

title: Cilium 1.16 renames, relabels or removes Prometheus metrics — dashboards and alerts that query them go blank

detection.reason: Prometheus series names are not Kubernetes objects; runtimez does not scrape Cilium metrics

quote: Metrics `policy_regeneration_total` and `policy_regeneration_time_stats_seconds` have been deprecated
remediation: Before upgrading to 1.16, search your dashboards, recording rules and alerts for the metric names listed in the Cilium 1.16 upgrade notes (Changed / Removed Metrics) and move them to the new names or labels. An alert on a renamed or removed series does not fail: it silently stops firing.
coversNotes: Changed Metrics: The `cilium_api_limiter_processed_requests_total` has now label `return_code`
